method.inference: None. Cached probabilities only; each cache's rows_sha256 is checked against the rows file before it is used.
method.scope: ML tier only. Rules tier and semantic veto are excluded, so these are not product recall/FPR -- the product path scores differently in both directions.
method.unmeasurable: A criterion this set cannot measure is reported UNMEASURABLE and is never counted as a pass.

cpu_p95_as_deployed_dynamic_padding.note: p95 of batch-one CPU inference with dynamic padding, which is what production runs: onnxBackend.ts:346 defaults dynamicPadding to true and no env file overrides it.

cpu_p95_fixed256_counterfactual.note: p95 if every input were padded to the full 256-token window, i.e. what ML_ONNX_DYNAMIC_PADDING=off would cost. Reported to bound the worst case, not as the deployed configuration.

input_window.note: MEASURED at 4,096 content tokens through the real backend (long-input-latency-2026-09-23.json), and it fails three independent ways. (1) As deployed (sliding window off) p95 is 304.076ms while only 6.2% of the input is scored - the rest is truncated before the forward pass, so this is not a 4k-token latency figure even though it is over budget anyway. (2) Turning the sweep on raises coverage to 37.9% across 24 windows and costs 2458.252ms, 49x the target. (3) A 4k-token input is refused before any tier sees it: MAX_GUARD_TEXT_LENGTH is 8000 chars, measured at ~1384 content tokens on this tokenizer. The 256-token window is architectural, not a flag: closing this needs a longer-context encoder.

1_latency.caveat: Inference only. Excludes tokenization, rules tier, semantic veto and transport. The input_window part is the exception: it calls backend.infer() directly, so its figures INCLUDE tokenization, which is O(chars) and is why its cost still rises with input length while the forward pass stays constant.

2_strongest_in_market.note: No competitor has been scored on these rows. A head-to-head needs each competitor run through this same battery and decision contract.
2_strongest_in_market.history: ProtectAI's DeBERTa has previously beaten SoterAI on a like-for-like corpus; the in-repo ranking docs asserting otherwise were withdrawn.

f1.note: Binary attack-vs-safe F1 at the evaluated gate.

auc_roc.note: Threshold-free, on P(attack)=1-P(SAFE). Independent of the gate.

multi-turn / context accumulation.note: ['MULTI_TURN_ESCALATION'] is detected by the model but excluded from the INPUT allowlist in lib/guard/mlAugment.ts, so production discards it: the measured recall is not enforced.

payload splitting.note: No taxonomy label expresses this family, so no row can evidence coverage.

4_attack_coverage.note: A family passes only when it has enough rows to measure, is admitted to the production INPUT allowlist, and clears the recall floor.

languages_present.note: Distinct annotated languages with any row in this battery.

languages_with_benign_rows.note: Languages carrying at least one benign row. Below this count, per-language FPR cannot be measured at all, whatever the attack-side coverage says.

5_languages.note: Eval-set coverage only. Training-corpus language coverage is a separate claim and is not evidenced by this file. FLORES-200 is not used here.

6_recall_and_fpr.note: Reported together on the same rows at the same gate, as the spec requires.

ood_layer.note: Artifact ships an out-of-distribution entropy budget consumed by the abstention path.

continual_learning.note: The loop is now CONNECTED end to end: lib/guard/persistence.ts calls recordGuardObservation() on every guard decision (one choke point, so a new route cannot silently miss it), rows travel over a Redis list, and the worker's harvest tier drains that same queue (tests/continuous-learning-intake.test.ts proves the round trip, including that a row is popped exactly once and that a queued row cannot claim a TRUSTED source). It is still FAIL because CONTINUOUS_LEARNING is not 'on' in any real env file, so nothing is collected in production. Model WEIGHTS remain out of scope for the worker by design (tier 4 needs a GPU and a shadow window), so this criterion tops out at 'the loop runs and quarantines candidates', never 'the model retrains itself unattended'.

language_recall_spread.note: max-min recall spread across 8 languages with >= 30 attack rows.

reproducible.note: Rows, model, tokenizer, calibration and decision-layer digests all recorded.

deployment_blockers: Labels ['DATA_EXFILTRATION_ATTEMPT', 'MULTI_TURN_ESCALATION', 'TOXICITY_HARASSMENT'] appear as attacks in this battery but are absent from the INPUT allowlist, so the ML tier's detections for them are discarded (gatedBy="label-family") and no retraining can raise ML recall for those families. Product impact is smaller than that sounds: the rules tier runs first and catches most of these rows, so widening the allowlist must be measured on the real path (scripts/ml/measure-gate-widening.ts), never from ML-tier pricing alone - on v14 the two differed by 37x.
